claim.quote: At a WIMP mass of 50 GeV/c^2, WIMP-nucleon spin-independent cross sections above 2.2e-46 cm^2 are excluded at the 90% confidence level. When combined with the previously reported LUX exposure, this exclusion strengthens to 1.1e-46 cm^2 at 50 GeV/c^2.

date.note: arXiv v1 submission date (preprint). Published as Phys. Rev. Lett. 118, 021303 (2017).

key_value.note: Combined WS2013 + WS2014-16 spin-independent WIMP-nucleon limit at 90% CL and 50 GeV/c². The WS2014-16 exposure alone gives 2.2e-46 cm².
key_value.quote: this exclusion strengthens to 1.1e-46 cm^2 at 50 GeV/c^2

key_value_text.quote: WIMP-nucleon spin-independent cross sections above 2.2e-46 cm^2 are excluded at the 90% confidence level
key_value_text.value: 1.1×10⁻⁴⁶ cm² spin-independent WIMP–nucleon cross section at 90% CL and 50 GeV/c² for the complete LUX exposure (2.2×10⁻⁴⁶ cm² for WS2014-16 alone)

name: Results from a search for dark matter in the complete LUX exposure
notes: significance is null: this is an exclusion limit.

summary.plain: Using all the data LUX ever took, the team again found no sign of dark matter and set limits about four times tighter than their earlier ones for heavy dark matter particles.
summary.technical: Complete LUX exposure: 3.35e4 kg day (WS2013 85.3 live days plus WS2014-16 332.0 live days, 11 Sep 2014 - 2 May 2016) with 250 kg active mass. No WIMP nuclear recoils; 90% CL spin-independent limit 2.2e-46 cm2 at 50 GeV/c2, strengthening to 1.1e-46 cm2 when combined with WS2013.

title: Results from a search for dark matter in the complete LUX exposure
why_it_matters: The final LUX exposure was the strongest direct-detection limit before the multi-tonne generation, and set the bar that LZ was built to beat.
